stem: Engr. Santos has just assumed a government post. She is a board member and a substantial stockholder of a private construction company whose interests may be affected by her official duties, so a conflict of interest arises. Under Section 9 of RA 6713, what must she do?
choices: Resign from the company within 30 days and divest her shares within 60 days of assuming office
Resign from the company within 60 days and divest her shares within 30 days of assuming office
Resign from the company and divest her shares within one year of assuming office
Declare the shares in her SALN; she need not resign or divest
answer: Resign from the company within 30 days and divest her shares within 60 days of assuming office
hints: Section 9 sets two different deadlines: one for leaving her position in the company, and one for giving up her shares.
Both deadlines are counted from her assumption of office. The deadline for resigning is the shorter one.
When a conflict of interest arises, Section 9 asks for action, not just disclosure. Recall which deadline is 30 days and which is 60 days, and match each to resigning or divesting.

solution.methodName: Match each number to its rule

steps.action: Check that there is a conflict of interest. Section 3(i) says it arises when an official is "a member of a board, an officer, or a substantial stockholder of a private corporation" whose interest "may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty." Engr. Santos fits.
steps.why: A substantial stockholder owns enough shares to elect a director of the company (Section 3(f)).

steps.action: Read Section 9: "When a conflict of interest arises, he shall resign from his position in any private business enterprise within thirty (30) days from his assumption of office and/or divest himself of his shareholdings or interest within sixty (60) days from such assumption."
steps.why: To divest means to give up ownership, for example by transferring the shares to someone who is not her spouse or relative (Section 3(j)).

steps.action: Match the numbers: resign from the board within 30 days; divest the shares within 60 days.

Read "and/or": she must resign if the conflict comes from her position, divest if it comes from her shares, or do both if it comes from both. Engr. Santos is a board member and a substantial stockholder, and Section 3(i) makes each one a source of conflict, so she must do both.
steps.why: Resigning alone would leave her a substantial stockholder, and divesting alone would leave her on the board. Either way the conflict would remain.

steps.action: Rule out declaring the shares in her SALN only: Section 9 requires her to resign and/or divest. Disclosure alone does not remove the conflict.
The answer is: Resign from the company within 30 days and divest her shares within 60 days of assuming office.

trapNotes.Resign from the company within 60 days a: The numbers are swapped. Section 9 gives 30 days to resign from the position and 60 days to divest the shares.
trapNotes.Resign from the company and divest her s: One year is the Section 7(b) period after leaving office. Section 9 gives 30 days to resign and 60 days to divest.
trapNotes.Declare the shares in her SALN; she need: Section 9 requires action, not just disclosure: when a conflict of interest arises, she "shall resign" from her position "and/or divest" her shares within the set deadlines. As a board member and a substantial stockholder, she must do both.
